subject: Request for short-term data retention window for live debugging
messages:
From: Asha Pillai <asha.pillai@acmeanalytics.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent failures — request for retained traces

Hi Neha / Rishi,

We saw a production spike this morning tied to our ingestion pipeline (user org: Acme Analytics, sample user id: acct-27f9). The service returned 500s for a subset of requests and our engineering team could really use the original traces/requests to correlate with our side.

Is there a supported way to temporarily retain the full request/response traces (including token-level traces) for 48 hours for debugging? We understand retention defaults are short, but without the raw traces we can't reproduce the failure.

I've attached a small sample context that shows the failing request flow. Happy to sign any exception forms you need.

Thanks,
Asha
Asha Pillai
Technical Program Manager, Acme Analytics
asha.pillai@acmeanalytics.com
Attachment: sample-failure-ctx.txt
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Re: Intermittent failures — request for retained traces

Looping infra & security. Customer (Acme) is requesting an exception to retention for a live debugging session.

Quick context: they reported intermittent 500s at ~08:45 PT. They want token-level traces for 48 hours. I started a retention_override form but need approvals. What is the minimal set we can grant so engineering can triage while keeping compliance happy?

Proposed immediate steps from support:
- Fill retention_override_form.docx (I can do)
- Limit access to explicitly named engineers
- Timebox the window (48h preferred by customer)

Can engineering confirm whether a narrower subset (e.g., only request headers + error KV) would suffice? If we need full traces we'll need signoff.

-Rishi
Senior Support Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Intermittent failures — request for retained traces

Thanks — quick follow. Engineering needs enough context to reproduce the error which in this case appears tied to prompt length + a rare cache invalidation. From past incidents, partial traces (headers + error payload) are often insufficient. We would prefer a 72h window, but we can accept 48h if Security/Legal require it.

If we proceed, here's the least-privilege plan I propose:
- Snapshot the exact requests for the affected time range only (time-bounded query).
- Store them in a secured S3 bucket with customer-specific prefix and server-side encryption (KMS key redwood-debug-rotating).
- Grant access to two named engineers: vivek_kulkarni and jordan_blake (engineering lead on the incident) and one on-call support (rishi_malhotra).
- No PII export; redact any fields matching the PII regex (email, ssn-like patterns) before any copy leaves the bucket.
- Audit log enabled for all reads; rotate the KMS key immediately after the window.

If Legal/Security sign off on those controls we can snapshot ASAP.

On Fri, 12 Jun 2026 at 09:12, Asha Pillai <asha.pillai@acmeanalytics.com> wrote:
> Hi Neha / Rishi,
> 
> We saw a production spike this morning tied to our ingestion pipeline...
> Attachment: sample-failure-ctx.txt

Vivek
Senior Software Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Intermittent failures — request for retained traces

Appreciate the low-privilege plan, Vivek. A few security/PD concerns to surface before we grant any exception:

1) Data residency: Acme is US-only, but the snapshot must be pinned to a US region bucket (no cross-region replication).
2) PII: We need an explicit redaction checklist. If we cannot deterministically redact certain fields, we should limit to metadata-level traces only.
3) Auditability: All accesses must be logged and immutable for the retention period; provide a JIRA ticket reference for the debugging work.
4) Key handling: KMS key rotation is required post-window and we need proof of rotation.

Please attach the completed retention_override_form_filled.pdf and a short justification note (who, why, what) so we have an audit trail. I will not approve full token-level exports without Legal signoff.

--
Dylan Brooks
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: retention_override_form_filled.pdf
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 13 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Intermittent failures — request for retained traces

I've reviewed the proposed controls and the filled exception form. Legal can approve a 48-hour exception on the following conditions:

- Scope limited to the specific request IDs/time window identified by Acme; no open-ended exports.
- Access list limited to: vivek_kulkarni, jordan_blake (please add jordan to this thread if required), and rishi_malhotra.
- Obligate redaction of PII before any artifact is shared outside Redwood. If redaction cannot be guaranteed, data must remain in the encrypted bucket and be accessed only from an approved debug VM.
- Signed exception confirmation from the customer (DocuSign link below).
- Security to produce audit logs and KMS rotation proof to Legal within 72 hours of window close.

DocuSign (customer sign-off): https://app.docusign.com/EXAMPLE/ABC-9876
JIRA tracking: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4823

Once the DocuSign confirmation is returned, Security may enable the snapshot for 48 hours.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Asha Pillai <asha.pillai@acmeanalytics.com>, Jared Collins <jared.collins@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Request for short-term data retention window for live debugging

Hi Asha / Jared — thanks for your patience. Quick status and next steps: 

1) Legal has conditionally approved a 48-hour retention window starting now (2026-06-14T16:00:00Z) for the specific request IDs you provided. Please return the signed DocuSign exception (link below) to finalize.
2) Security will capture a time-bounded snapshot and store it in a US-only encrypted bucket (prefix: acme-debug/acct-27f9/). Access will be granted only to: vivek_kulkarni and jordan_blake (engineering) and rishi_malhotra (support) once customer sign-off is received.
3) Engineering will perform redaction of PII fields before any artifact is exported; if redaction cannot be fully automated, access will be restricted to an approved debug VM.
4) Audit logs and KMS rotation proof will be delivered to Legal within 72 hours after the window closes.

DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/EXAMPLE/ABC-9876
JIRA: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4823

Asha — please confirm you can sign within the hour so we can proceed. If you prefer a 72h window, let us know and we will reopen Legal.

Thanks everyone for quick coordination.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Principal PM, Trust & Safety, Redwood Inference
